fixes.explanation: Right at the gate, baker. God says, "Stand in the gate of the house of the LORD and proclaim this message…" (Jeremiah 7:2). Then He tells Jeremiah who to address: "…all you people of Judah who enter through these gates to worship the LORD." That's a message with a very clear address on it.

The treasury is a good guess for a temple spot, but it's not what the verse says. God tells Jeremiah to stand "…in the gate of the house of the LORD…" (Jeremiah 7:2). The message is for the people of Judah who enter through those gates to worship. Me, I'd have guessed the treasury too, and I'd have been just as wrong.

A storeroom is a fine spot for keeping things, but it's not where God sends Jeremiah. God says to stand "…in the gate of the house of the LORD…" (Jeremiah 7:2). The message is for "…all you people of Judah who enter through these gates to worship the LORD." The gate is the spot God picked.

This one is true, friend. The text says, "Correct your ways and deeds, and I will let you live in this place." (Jeremiah 7:3). God starts the message with the way forward. Don't let the stern tone later on hide that.

You've got it, friend. God says, "…if you act justly toward one another…" (Jeremiah 7:5). He's talking about how they treat each other, not just how they act when they come to worship. The list that follows gets even more specific.

Yep. God asks if they will come stand before Him in His house and say, "We are delivered, so we can continue with all these abominations…" (Jeremiah 7:10). Read that slowly. It's a get-out-of-trouble card, with the permission to keep going built right in. God holds up that picture and asks if it makes sense.

I wish that was the line, friend. But sorry and ready to change is the opposite of what God puts in their mouths. The words in His question are, "We are delivered, so we can continue with all these abominations…" (Jeremiah 7:10). That's a very different speech.

Needing His help would be a different conversation entirely. The words God puts in His question are, "We are delivered, so we can continue with all these abominations…" (Jeremiah 7:10). That's about feeling safe and carrying on. Nothing in the verse about being poor.

That's the one. God asks, "Has this house, which bears My Name, become a den of robbers in your sight?" (Jeremiah 7:11). Then He adds, "Yes, I too have seen it…" That's the picture He chooses, and He says He has seen it too.

Lions have a den, sure, but that's not the picture here. God asks, "Has this house, which bears My Name, become a den of robbers in your sight?" (Jeremiah 7:11). Robbers, not lions. I'd have been scared of the lions, honestly.
